title: Quickstarts Adoption KPIs (Hosted API) — draft sheet
content:
TAB: Summary
Last updated: 2025-03-14 (Nikhil)

Goal
Define a KPI + telemetry spec to measure whether Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) improve Hosted API activation, conversion, and reduce support load, without collecting sensitive content.

Scope
- Hosted API self-serve + sales-assisted (but metrics primarily PLG).
- Template-originated traffic only (tagged / identifiable).
- Initial templates: rag-agent-python, rag-agent-typescript.

North Star (v1)
- Time-to-First-Success (TTFS): from first API key created to first successful template-run request (200 + stream completed OR non-stream response completed) within 60 minutes.

Primary KPIs
1) Activation
- TTFS (p50/p90) for template users vs non-template new users
- Activation rate: % of new accounts reaching “First Success” within D0 (same day) / D7

2) Conversion
- % of activated template users converting to paid within 14/30 days
- $: first 30-day revenue per activated template account (median)

3) Retention / quality of adoption
- D7/D30 retention: % of activated template accounts with >= X tokens / >= Y requests
- Share of traffic tagged as template-originated for first 7 days (proxy for “stuck with it”)

4) Support deflection
- Support tickets per 1k new accounts (template cohort vs baseline)
- Template troubleshooting page engagement vs ticket creation (proxy)

Guardrails
- Opt-in telemetry by default for non-essential headers; templates must still function if telemetry is disabled.
- No prompts, completions, retrieved documents, or tool outputs in analytics events.
- Avoid high-cardinality dimensions (don’t log raw request IDs, customer IDs in metrics tags; use internal joins).

Owners
- KPI definitions + targets: Nikhil (Hosted API PM), Henry (Hosted API PM)
- Telemetry platform + analytics plumbing: Logan Wright
- Template implementation: Monica Patel (DevEx)
- Docs funnel + troubleshooting instrumentation: Elliot Price (Docs), Wei Chen (Tech writer)
- Support deflection measurement: Priya Shah (Support feedback loop), Dev Patel (Support ops)


TAB: KPI Definitions

KPI 1 — Time-to-First-Success (TTFS)
Definition
- Start: timestamp of first API key created OR first successful auth handshake (whichever is available reliably in data warehouse).
- End: timestamp of first “template_success” event OR first “api_request_success” with template tag + completion/stream end.

Inclusion criteria
- Accounts created after template launch date.
- Template cohort identified by either:
  (a) CLI init event (qs.cli.init)
  (b) template app event (qs.app.start) with template metadata
  (c) API traffic containing template tag header (see telemetry section)

Success condition
- Any generation/embedding request that returns 200 AND is not immediately followed by a client-abort flagged error. For streaming:
  - Success = stream completed (client received end-of-stream) OR server sent a final chunk.

Reporting
- p50/p90 TTFS by: template_name, language, sdk (py/ts), region (bucketed), and plan type (free/paid)


KPI 2 — Activation rate
Definition
- Activation event: first_success
- Rate D0: % of new accounts that reach first_success within 24 hours of signup.
- Rate D7: % within 7 days.

Activation funnel stages (see “Funnel Events” tab)
- signup_created
- api_key_created
- template_scaffolded
- local_run_started
- first_success
- deployed_success (optional, later)


KPI 3 — Conversion to paid
Definition
- % of accounts in template cohort converting to paid plan within 14 and 30 days of signup.
- Also track: time from first_success -> paid conversion (p50/p90).

Notes
- Separate self-serve paid vs sales-assisted contract conversions.
- For sales-assisted, treat “opportunity created” as intermediate metric.


KPI 4 — Retention / sustained usage
Definition
- D7 retention: activated accounts with >= 10 successful requests OR >= 200k tokens by day 7.
- D30 retention: activated accounts with >= 50 successful requests OR >= 1M tokens by day 30.

Rationale
- We want to avoid counting “one-and-done” template runs as success.
- Thresholds should be revisited after internal beta baselines.


KPI 5 — Support deflection
Definition
- Ticket rate: (# support tickets created by accounts in cohort within first 14 days) / (# accounts in cohort) * 1000
- Compare to baseline cohort (new accounts same time window, non-template identified).

Ticket taxonomy (initial)
- auth (401)
- quota/rate limit (429)
- networking/timeout
- streaming disconnect
- otel exporter/config
- tool schema validation
- retrieval empty/poor relevance

Success metric
- Reduce ticket rate by 15–25% for template cohort vs baseline within 60 days of public launch.


TAB: Funnel Events (Event dictionary)

Conventions
- Prefix “qs.” = template/quickstart specific events
- Prefix “api.” = already-existing API traffic events, with added template tags/dimensions

Required fields for qs.* events
- template_name (enum; e.g., rag-agent)
- template_language (python|typescript)
- template_version (semver string)
- distribution (cli|github)
- telemetry_opt_in (true|false)
- environment (local|ci|prod) — keep as small enum

Event table

| Event name | When fired | Source | Required properties | Optional properties (bounded) | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qs.cli.install | CLI installed | CLI | os (mac|linux|windows), arch (x64|arm64) | shell (zsh|bash|fish) | Monica | If we can’t reliably capture, drop. Useful to debug install friction. |
| qs.cli.init | Template scaffolded | CLI | template_name, template_language, template_version, distribution=cli | git_init (true|false) | Monica | Writes a local “version stamp” file; event only if telemetry_opt_in=true. |
| qs.cli.doctor | Doctor run | CLI | template_name, template_language, template_version | checks_failed_count (0-10), primary_failure (enum) | Monica | primary_failure: missing_api_key|bad_model|collector_unreachable|dns|other |
| qs.app.start | App started | App | template_name, template_language, template_version, environment=local | runtime (node|python), framework (fastapi|express|other) | Monica | Used to measure “got it running”. |
| qs.app.first_request | First user request made in app | App | template_name, template_language, template_version | request_kind (chat|embed|rerank), used_retrieval (true|false) | Monica | Avoid logging user input. Just the action category. |
| qs.app.first_success | First successful completion/stream | App | template_name, template_language, template_version | streaming (true|false), used_tools (true|false) | Monica | This is preferred “First Success” marker; fallback to api.request success if missing. |
| qs.app.error | Template error surfaced to user | App | template_name, template_language, template_version, error_category (enum) | http_status (200/400/401/429/5xx), retry_attempted (true|false) | Monica + Priya | error_category aligns with template error taxonomy; keep stable for support. |
| api.request | Any API request | Gateway/SDK | request_id (internal), customer_account_id (internal) | template_tag (string), template_version (string) | Logan | Template tag should be join key for cohorting; do not create high-cardinality metrics tags. |
| api.request.success | Successful API request | Gateway/SDK | status=200 | latency_bucket (enum), tokens_in_bucket (enum), tokens_out_bucket (enum) | Logan | Use buckets to avoid cardinality issues. |
| api.request.error | Failed API request | Gateway/SDK | status (401|429|5xx|timeout) | error_type (enum), retryable (true|false) | Logan | Align with SDK error types. |

Template tag header proposal (for api.* attribution)
- Header: X-Redwood-Template
  - Value: <template_name>@<template_version>;<language>
  - Example: rag-agent@1.1.0;python
- Header: X-Redwood-Template-Opt-In
  - Value: true|false

Notes
- Headers must be optional. Some corporate proxies reject unknown headers; templates should support disabling via env.
- Gateway allowlist required (see linked PRs). If blocked, templates should still work and fall back to qs.* events only (if any).


TAB: Dashboard Spec (What we want in Console/Analytics)

Dashboard 1: Quickstarts Overview
- New accounts (daily)
- Template cohort size (daily)
- Activation rate D0/D7 (template vs baseline)
- TTFS p50/p90 (template vs baseline)
- Top failure categories (qs.app.error) by count

Dashboard 2: Funnel (Template cohort)
- api_key_created -> qs.cli.init -> qs.app.start -> first_success
- Drop-off % at each step
- Median time between steps

Dashboard 3: Reliability + cost signals (Template-tagged traffic)
- 401 rate, 429 rate, 5xx rate
- streaming disconnect rate (if detectable via SDK / client abort signals)
- Latency p50/p95 (bucketed)
- Tokens out per request (bucketed)

Dashboard 4: Support deflection
- Tickets per 1k new accounts (template vs baseline)
- Ticket breakdown by category
- Link-outs: troubleshooting docs views, “helpfulness” votes (if available)

Operational view (internal)
- Filter in Console for template-tagged traffic (required for triage + demos)
- Ability to pivot by template_name + version (low cardinality only)


TAB: Targets (initial strawman; to revisit post-internal beta)

Assumptions
- Templates are production-minded; primary value is reducing onboarding entropy and failure loops.

Targets (first 60–90 days post public launch)
- TTFS p50 <= 20 minutes for template cohort (from api_key_created)
- Activation D0: +10–15pp vs baseline
- Activation D7: +5–10pp vs baseline
- Conversion to paid (30d): +2–4pp vs baseline (small early expectation)
- Support tickets per 1k new accounts: -15% vs baseline

What “baseline” means
- New accounts in same time window that do not have template tags or qs.* events.


TAB: Implementation Notes / Constraints

Privacy
- Do not log prompts, retrieved text, tool inputs/outputs, file paths.
- For error events, include category + short stable error_code only (no full stack traces in analytics).

Cardinality constraints
- Allowed dimensions for dashboards: template_name, template_version (top N only), language, environment, status code, error_category.
- Not allowed as metric labels: account_id, request_id, raw model name if too granular (use “model_family” bucket where needed).

Data quality concerns (known)
- Some users scaffold via GitHub template without CLI; we need API-level attribution via headers.
- Some proxies block headers; telemetry should be resilient/optional.
- Streaming “success” is tricky; we need consistent detection (SDK improvements in flight).

Dependencies
- CLI emits qs.cli.init / qs.cli.doctor (DevEx)
- SDK/gateway header allowlist + safe handling (Platform)
- Console filter for template-tagged traffic (Console/Analytics)
- Support ticket tagging alignment with taxonomy (Support Ops)


TAB: Open Questions
1) TTFS start timestamp source
- API key created is best but not always tied to “first attempt”. Alternative: first 401/200 request timestamp.

2) Opt-in defaults
- Do we default telemetry_opt_in=true for template events but make header tagging opt-in? (current leaning: yes; reduce proxy issues)

3) GitHub template attribution
- If user clones repo, we can still set X-Redwood-Template by default from app config. But we need an obvious “turn off telemetry” switch.

4) Defining “paid conversion” for sales-assisted
- Use opportunity created + stage progression? Or strict paid contract signature only?

5) Support deflection attribution window
- 14 days vs 30 days. Support suggests 14 days captures most onboarding tickets; keep both in reporting.

6) Regions / deployment modes
- For hosted API metrics, we can bucket by region. For Dedicated/Private, separate dashboards later.

Change log
- 2025-02-07: Added support deflection definitions + ticket taxonomy mapping.
- 2025-02-21: Updated template header proposal to be optional due to proxy/header issues found in early trials.
- 2025-03-14: Added funnel step definitions (qs.app.first_success preferred over api.request.success for streaming correctness).
